entries.note: PMID 15118073, epub 2004-04-29, same day as Paez (PMID 15118125). Mutations sequenced from 8/9 responders, then expressed in cells: patient-to-model. No patient target-engagement measured, so untested holds on both grounds.

Cross 2014 (epub 2014-06-03) published the cell/xenograft/transgenic prediction incl. wild-type sparing before AURA (2015-04-30). 61% vs 21% is genotype-stratified response, not a PD readout (rule question 4). Cross 2014 already carried 2 T790M+ responders, so 2014 is arguable.

PMID 15897464, epub 2005-05-16, after Kobayashi (2005-02-24) and Pao (2005-02-22). Quote verbatim in abstract. Kwak tested HKI-272 (neratinib), EKB-569 and CL-387,785, not afatinib; note wording is fine.

Abstract verbatim except naive/naïve; 'No patients with known T790M responded' confirmed. Paper hedges ('potentially'); the claim that exposure fell below the H1975-defined level is not in the abstract and full text was not reachable. Confidence should be medium, not high.

Quote and no-DLT claim verified. The brief says validity belongs to the context and contra 'overrides every matched status'; it writes no reset on model change. The 2010 H1975 contradiction stands, so 2015 stays contra; record the osimertinib selectivity match in judgement or drop the entry.

Quote is the abstract's final sentence. Patient-to-model direction confirmed. Rule 6 makes the first model year untested regardless, so the retrodiction call is consistent with the brief; the brief itself is silent on retrodiction (rule question 1).

PMID 16785471, epub 2006-06-19; 16 patients, ORR 75%, PFS 9.7 mo verified. Drop transgenic mice from `model`: Politi 2006 (epub 2006-05-16) postdates the trial's enrolment (2004-06 to 2005-10); the trial relied on the Lynch/Paez cell data plus the retrospective patient correlation.

Janjigian names the preclinical hypothesis ('first clinical proof-of-concept'). Regales 2009 (epub 2009-09-14) predates LUX-Lung 1 (2012). Regales full text: BIBW-2992 alone gave 0/7 CRs, 6 SD, and calls Li 2008 'modest activity' in T790M mice, so the drafter's 'stricter contra from 2012' alternative overstates Li 2008 (Li full text not read).

Inoue 2003 makes no model comparison. Label numbers verified (1.3%/2462, 0.7% ≥G3, 3 fatal, >2-fold exposure-ILD), but §13 holding only 13.1 is PLR format, not evidence of animal silence. Hama 2006 (10.4321/s1885-642x2006000400004) reports the 6-month dog study showed chronic pneumonia, alveolar macrophages, septal metaplasia and alveolar haemorrhage in gefitinib groups only, plus 3 interstitial pneumonia cases in 133 Japanese pre-approval patients. Premise contradicted; no primary source makes the comparison; rule 1 fails.

missing: safety: Hama 2006 (Pharm Pract 2006;4(4):168, PMC4155619, doi 10.4321/s1885-642x2006000400004) is the only published document found that juxtaposes animal lung findings with clinical ILD; it cites AstraZeneca's 2005-02-25 Japanese disclosure of the dog toxicology as the primary record. Cite it in the untested note, with the dog findings.

safety: if the 2003 contra falls, the osimertinib wild-type-sparing prediction (Cross 2014, 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-14-0337) versus AURA (Janne 2015: no DLT at 20-240 mg, diarrhoea/rash mostly low grade) is a candidate `same` in 2015; the Janne abstract does not make the tolerability comparison explicit, so check full text or the Tagrisso FDA review before scoring. Tagrisso label ILD (not fetched) would face the same rule-1 problem as gefitinib.

engagement: Cross 2014 itself reports 2 T790M+ patients as proof of principle (abstract: 'first published clinical proof-of-principle'); under rule 5 the first published comparison year for osimertinib is arguably 2014 (same paper, n=2) rather than 2015.

engagement/resistance: C797S. Ercan 2015 (10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-14-2789, epub 2015-05-06, ENU screen in Ba/F3 cells) vs Thress 2015 (10.1038/nm.3854, epub 2015-05-04, patient cfDNA). Simultaneous, patient paper two days earlier: not a clean prospective prediction; worth a line in judgement, not an entry.

dose: the Tagrisso 2015 FDA clinical pharmacology review would be the primary source for the exposure/selectivity-window comparison; neither drafter nor checker read it. The FDA 2003 Iressa review package index (drugsatfda_docs/nda/2003/021399_iressa.html) loads by script and could not be read; the 2003 label URL (label/2003/021399lbl.pdf) returned a redirect and was not verified.
rule_questions: Retrodiction: the brief does not say whether a same-paper patient-to-model comparison (Lynch/Paez 2004, Kobayashi/Pao 2005, Thress 2015) can be `same`. Rule 6 forces the first model year to untested anyway, so the draft is consistent, but the brief should state that a model built from the patient result is not a prediction.

Contra reset: the brief says validity belongs to the context and contra 'overrides every matched status', with no reset when the best model changes. As written, the dose cell cannot return to `same` in 2015 for osimertinib. If per-model stickiness is intended, the brief needs a line saying so.

Rule 1 and juxtaposition: whether a drafter may construct the comparison from two documents (a label's nonclinical section plus a clinical case series). As written, no: the source must make the comparison. The brief should also say that a PLR label omitting section 13.2 is not evidence that animal studies were silent.
Engagement proxy: whether genotype-stratified response (T790M-positive 61% vs negative 21%) counts as 'the drug hit its target in patients' when no PD or occupancy measurement was published.

`neg` scope: whether a drug that failed in one sub-population of the context (afatinib monotherapy after TKI failure, LUX-Lung 1 OS HR 1.08) but succeeded in another (first-line sensitising mutations) counts as 'went on to fail in patients'.

Dose `contra` vs `untested`: when toxicity stops patients reaching the model-defined exposure (neratinib diarrhoea), is the model's exposure target contradicted or merely untested? The draft reads it as contra; defensible, but the brief does not decide it.

Weak animal signal: whether a sponsor-dismissed finding (chronic pneumonia and alveolar changes in a 6-month dog study) followed by the clinical AE counts as the model having predicted it (`same`), or stays `untested` because no published source scored it as a prediction before the clinical signal.
